title: Sunny and the Night Bird's Song | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the Quokka follows the sound of an unseen bird singing one long, gentle note from somewhere deep in the moonlit bush — a sound that fills the whole night like a lullaby. A peaceful bedtime story for toddlers from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
The song started very quietly.

Sunny was already nearly asleep beneath a stringybark tree when she heard it — one long, soft note, rising and then falling, from somewhere deep in the bush.

She opened her eyes.

The note came again. The same one. Pure and clear and unhurried.

She could not see the bird. She looked and looked — into the high branches, along the dark creek bank, across the silver grass — but there was nothing. Just the song.

One note. Rising. Falling. A pause.

Then again.

It was the most peaceful sound Sunny had ever heard. Not joyful exactly. Not sad. Just... present. Like the bird was simply announcing: I am here. The night is here. Everything is all right.

Sunny lay back down. She stopped looking and just listened.

The note came and came and came — steady and gentle as a heartbeat. The whole bush seemed to organise itself around it. The crickets quieted. The breeze eased. Even the creek seemed to murmur more softly.

The song went on.

Sunny's breathing slowed to match it. In with the rising note. Out with the falling one.

She did not hear when the song stopped. She was already too far into sleep.

The bird sang on until the first pale light of morning.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, night bird. Goodnight, little one.
